name: Sophocles
summary: Sophocles was an ancient Greek tragedian, one of three from whom at least two plays have survived in full.

facts.text: Sophocles was an ancient Greek tragedian, one of three from whom at least two plays have survived in full.
facts.context: Sophocles's background gives readers a concrete entry point into Literature, Arts & Culture.

facts.text: Sophocles's first plays were written later than, or contemporary with, those of Aeschylus and earlier than, or contemporary with, those of Euripides.
facts.context: Sophocles's challenge makes the card about pressure and choice, not just fame.

facts.text: Sophocles wrote more than 120 plays, but only seven have survived in a complete form: Ajax, Antigone, Women of Trachis, Oedipus Rex, Electra, Philoctetes, and Oedipus at Colonus.
facts.context: Sophocles's turning point shows how one moment can redirect a public life.

facts.text: For almost 50 years, Sophocles was the most celebrated playwright in the dramatic competitions of the city-state of Athens, which took place during the religious festivals of the Lenaea and the Dionysia.
facts.context: Sophocles's contribution helps explain why this profile belongs in the People Library.

facts.text: Sophocles competed in 30 competitions, won 24, and was never judged lower than second place.
facts.context: Sophocles's influence connects one short Fact to a wider historical ripple.
